methods.label: Separate the generations
methods.explanation:
First separate Bertha’s daughters from her granddaughters. Since she has \(6\) daughters, she has
\[
30-6=24
\]
granddaughters. Each daughter who has daughters has exactly \(6\), so \(24\div6=4\) of Bertha’s daughters have daughters. The remaining \(6-4=2\) have none.

All \(24\) granddaughters have no daughters, because any such daughter would be Bertha’s great-granddaughter. Thus the required count is
\[
2+24=\boxed{26},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
